title: The Weekly Outreach System
subtitle: A 30-Minute Friday Routine for Introverted Professionals Who Need Warm Introductions Without Networking Events
promise: In four weeks you will run a 30-minute Friday outreach routine that produces warm introductions without attending a single networking event.
reader_profile: Dana is 44, an independent HR consultant two years into her practice, who just lost the client that paid half her bills. She has 400 LinkedIn connections, has never asked anyone for an introduction, and dreads events. She has tried posting on LinkedIn and joining a chamber of commerce; neither produced a client. She fears looking desperate to people who knew her when she was doing well. By the last page she wants a short weekly routine she can run alone at her desk that puts her in front of two new prospects a month.
positioning: Comps on networking teach events, elevator pitches, and personal branding, and their low reviews complain that the advice assumes an extrovert with free evenings. This book is a desk routine with a fixed time box, a message template, and a tracking sheet, written for people who would rather send five messages than walk into a room.

frameworks.name: The Friday Five
frameworks.summary: Five short, specific messages sent every Friday morning to people you already know.

frameworks.name: Warmth Ladder
frameworks.summary: Four rungs that move a contact from dormant to referral source: reconnect, help, ask, introduce.

frameworks.name: Ask Ledger
frameworks.summary: A one-page log of every ask, its answer, and the follow-up date.

tone: Plain, direct, practical; grade 8 reading level
reader_job: A reader hires this book to run a weekly outreach routine so they can get warm introductions to prospects without networking events.
outcome: A routine running every Friday, a list of 40 contacts placed on the Warmth Ladder, and an Ask Ledger with at least ten logged asks.
examples: Illustrative composite: Dana's first Friday Five, sent to five former colleagues, two replies within a day
Illustrative composite: a residential plumber who logged 12 asks in an Ask Ledger and learned that past customers, not other trades, sent him work
Illustrative composite: a bookkeeper who moved a dormant former manager up the Warmth Ladder over six weeks
Illustrative composite: an engineer turned consultant who replaced one monthly event with the Friday Five and kept the time
